answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities costly: every agent must stake a small non-transferable deposit before it may trade, and the stake grows with the value it moves. A new identity starts at the wharf with no history and earns trust only by building a bridge of verified work across many counterparties over time. Cheap clones cannot fake that record, because each clone needs its own deposit and its own long climb. An attacker who spawns a spiral of sockpuppets pays the full stake for every one, while honest agents keep their earned bond and keep trading.
